questions.explanation: The Sorting Hat's magic allows the sword to come to any Gryffindor who proves themselves worthy in a crisis.

questions.question_text: What does Narcissa Malfoy ask Harry, quietly, in the forest just before falsely telling Voldemort that he is dead?
questions.correct_answer: Whether Draco is still alive inside Hogwarts
distractors: Whether Voldemort truly loves her family
Whether Harry knows where Lucius is
Whether the war is truly over
questions.explanation: Narcissa's only real concern is her son's survival, prompting her to lie to Voldemort for Harry's sake.

questions.question_text: Why does Voldemort mistakenly believe that killing Snape will make him the Elder Wand's true master?
questions.correct_answer: He assumes ownership passes by killing the previous holder, rather than by disarming them
distractors: He believes the wand chooses its master at random
He thinks only blood relatives of Dumbledore can wield it
He believes Snape had already surrendered the wand's loyalty to him
questions.explanation: Voldemort misunderstands the wand's lore, not realizing Snape was never its true master to begin with.

questions.question_text: How does Harry, rather than anyone else, ultimately become the Elder Wand's true master before the final duel?
questions.correct_answer: By having disarmed Draco Malfoy at Malfoy Manor earlier in the story
distractors: By defeating Voldemort in single combat first
By retrieving it personally from Dumbledore's tomb
questions.explanation: Harry's earlier duel with Draco, in which he disarmed him, secretly transferred the wand's true allegiance.

questions.question_text: What Ministry-created position gives Dolores Umbridge the power to inspect and potentially dismiss other Hogwarts teachers?
questions.explanation: An Educational Decree grants Umbridge sweeping authority to oversee and discipline the Hogwarts staff.

questions.question_text: What Ministry action bans all Hogwarts student clubs and societies without prior approval, ultimately exposing Dumbledore's Army?
questions.correct_answer: An Educational Decree outlawing unauthorized student organizations
distractors: A direct order from the Wizengamot
A ban issued by the school governors
A curfew imposed on all students
questions.explanation: The decree is specifically crafted to catch groups like the D.A., leading to its discovery.

questions.question_text: Which student betrays the existence and meeting place of Dumbledore's Army to Umbridge?
questions.explanation: Marietta reports the group to Umbridge, despite having signed the D.A.'s enchanted membership list.

questions.question_text: What does Hermione's hex do to the student who betrays Dumbledore's Army to Umbridge?
questions.correct_answer: Covers her face in painful pustules spelling out "SNEAK"
distractors: Makes her unable to speak for a week
questions.explanation: Hermione had jinxed the sign-up parchment to punish anyone who betrayed the group's secret.

questions.question_text: Which mostly-Slytherin group of students does Umbridge deputize with the power to dock house points and enforce her rules?
questions.explanation: Umbridge forms the Squad, led by Draco Malfoy, to help her control the student body.

questions.question_text: Which magical creatures drag Dolores Umbridge away into the Forbidden Forest after she gravely insults them?
questions.explanation: Umbridge's contempt for the centaurs provokes them into carrying her off, out of the story for the rest of the book.

questions.question_text: What insulting term does Umbridge use for the centaurs that provokes their attack on her?
questions.explanation: Her contempt for non-human magical beings, already evident throughout the book, boils over in the forest.

questions.question_text: What is the name of Hagrid's giant half-brother, secretly brought to live hidden in the Forbidden Forest?
questions.explanation: Hagrid brings Grawp back from his mission to the giants and hides him in the forest for safekeeping.

questions.question_text: What do Harry, Ron, and Hermione end up doing for Grawp during Hagrid's periodic absences?
questions.correct_answer: Trying to teach him English and keep him calm
distractors: Teaching him to fly a broom
Hiding him from the Ministry entirely
questions.explanation: Hagrid asks the trio to look in on his giant half-brother while he's away dealing with other matters.

questions.question_text: What is the outcome of Hagrid's secret mission to win the giants' allegiance for the Order of the Phoenix?
questions.correct_answer: It largely fails, as most giants side with Voldemort instead
distractors: It succeeds completely, securing an alliance
The giants turn on Voldemort's forces instead
questions.explanation: Hagrid returns injured and disappointed, having only won over a small faction of giants.

questions.question_text: Who takes over teaching Divination after Sybill Trelawney is publicly dismissed by Umbridge?
questions.explanation: Firenze agrees to teach at Hogwarts, offering a very different style of Divination than Trelawney's.

questions.question_text: What happens to Firenze as a direct consequence of agreeing to teach humans at Hogwarts?
questions.correct_answer: He is attacked and banished by his own herd
distractors: He is promoted to herd leader
He loses his ability to speak
He is welcomed back with honors
questions.explanation: The other centaurs see teaching humans as a betrayal, and Firenze is cast out for it.

questions.question_text: Why is Sybill Trelawney unable to be fully removed from the Hogwarts grounds despite Umbridge's dismissal?
questions.correct_answer: Dumbledore intervenes and allows her to keep living at the school
distractors: She refuses to leave and hides in the Astronomy Tower
Her contract cannot legally be broken by anyone but the Minister
questions.explanation: Though sacked as a teacher, Trelawney is permitted by Dumbledore to remain living at Hogwarts.

questions.question_text: What false vision does Voldemort implant in Harry's mind to lure him and his friends to the Ministry of Magic?
questions.correct_answer: That Sirius Black is being tortured there
distractors: That Voldemort himself is hiding there
That the Ministry is about to fall
questions.explanation: Voldemort deliberately plants the vision, knowing Harry will rush to save his godfather.

questions.question_text: What object shatters during the battle in the Death Chamber, destroying the only physical record of the prophecy?
questions.correct_answer: The glass orb containing the prophecy
questions.explanation: The orb falls and smashes amid the fighting, meaning the prophecy's exact wording is lost except to those who heard it.

questions.question_text: Whose curse causes Sirius Black to fall backward through the veiled archway to his death?
questions.explanation: Bellatrix strikes Sirius during their duel, and he tumbles through the mysterious veil, never to return.

questions.question_text: What does Harry attempt against Bellatrix Lestrange immediately after Sirius's death, which fails him?
questions.explanation: Harry's attempt at an Unforgivable Curse fails because he does not truly mean it with enough hatred.

questions.question_text: Who briefly takes control of Harry's body and mind during the Ministry confrontation with Dumbledore, exploiting his grief?
questions.explanation: Voldemort possesses Harry in a last attempt to manipulate Dumbledore, but Harry's love for Sirius helps him resist.

questions.question_text: What finally forces Cornelius Fudge to accept that Voldemort has truly returned?
questions.correct_answer: Seeing Voldemort with his own eyes at the Ministry Atrium
distractors: Seeing the Dark Mark on Lucius Malfoy's arm
questions.explanation: Fudge's denial finally collapses once Voldemort appears in front of him during the battle.

questions.question_text: Which Weasley sibling severs ties with his family over his loyalty to the Ministry during this period?
questions.explanation: Percy sides with the Ministry's official line and stops speaking to his family for some time.

questions.question_text: How do Fred and George Weasley make their final, dramatic exit from Hogwarts under Umbridge's rule?
questions.correct_answer: Setting off fireworks and flying away on brooms, quitting school for good
distractors: Being formally expelled by the Ministry
Being banished by Dumbledore's Army vote
questions.explanation: The twins stage a spectacular departure, leaving Umbridge's regime in chaos behind them.

questions.question_text: What parting "gift" do Fred and George leave behind in a school corridor to torment Umbridge?
questions.explanation: The corridor-wide swamp becomes a lasting monument to the twins' rebellion, one Filch can never fully remove.

questions.question_text: What happens to the Death Eaters captured at the Ministry battle within about a year of their imprisonment?
questions.correct_answer: Voldemort breaks them out of Azkaban
distractors: They are all given the Dementor's Kiss
They are quietly released by the Ministry
They remain imprisoned for the rest of the war
questions.explanation: Voldemort orchestrates a mass breakout, freeing his captured followers from Azkaban.
questions.source_ref: Order of the Phoenix / Half-Blood Prince

questions.question_text: What is unusual about how Sirius Black's death leaves no trace behind, unlike most deaths in the series?
questions.correct_answer: His body vanishes through the veiled archway
distractors: He is turned entirely to ash
His body is never recovered from the lake
questions.explanation: Sirius simply falls through the ancient veil and disappears, leaving Harry with no body to mourn over.

questions.question_text: Who physically restrains Harry from trying to follow Sirius through the veiled archway?
questions.explanation: Lupin holds Harry back, explaining that nothing can bring Sirius back from beyond the veil.

questions.question_text: Besides Harry, Ron, and Hermione, which three other students join the mission to "rescue" Sirius at the Ministry?
questions.explanation: The six students travel together to the Department of Mysteries, expecting to find Sirius in danger.

questions.question_text: Why does Dumbledore insist that Harry take Occlumency lessons from Snape during his fifth year?
questions.correct_answer: To prevent Voldemort from manipulating or spying through their mental connection
distractors: To help Harry improve his dueling skills
To prepare Harry for his O.W.L. exams
To help Harry control his temper
questions.explanation: Dumbledore worries Voldemort could plant false visions or read Harry's mind through their shared scar connection.

questions.question_text: What does Harry accidentally view in Snape's own Pensieve that causes Snape to end their Occlumency lessons for good?
questions.correct_answer: A private memory from Snape's own humiliating school days
distractors: A memory of Snape's initiation as a Death Eater
A memory of Lily Potter's death
A memory of Dumbledore's private plans
questions.explanation: Snape's fury at Harry's intrusion into his past ends the lessons abruptly, with lasting consequences.

questions.question_text: What does Harry witness through his scar connection to Voldemort that leads to a timely rescue of Arthur Weasley?
questions.correct_answer: A vision of Nagini attacking Mr. Weasley at the Ministry
distractors: A vision of Death Eaters raiding the Burrow
A vision of Umbridge attacking Mr. Weasley
A vision of Lucius Malfoy dueling Mr. Weasley
questions.explanation: Harry's vision, experienced as though he were Nagini himself, allows the Order to reach Arthur in time to save him.

questions.question_text: What ultimately happens to Cornelius Fudge's position as a consequence of his denial about Voldemort being exposed?
questions.correct_answer: He is forced to resign as Minister for Magic
distractors: He is arrested and sent to Azkaban
He is placed under the Imperius Curse
He remains Minister for the rest of the war
questions.explanation: Fudge's credibility collapses, and Rufus Scrimgeour takes over as Minister soon after.

questions.question_text: How does Harry's mental connection with Voldemort noticeably intensify throughout Order of the Phoenix, beyond simple scar pain?
questions.correct_answer: He begins sharing vivid visions, and even emotions, culminating in a brief possession
distractors: He begins losing his own memories to Voldemort
He starts speaking in Voldemort's voice involuntarily
He gains the ability to cast Voldemort's own signature spells
questions.explanation: The connection grows dangerously strong, worrying Dumbledore enough to insist on Occlumency lessons.

questions.question_text: What gift from Sirius does Harry neglect to use during his fifth year, only realizing its purpose too late to save him?
questions.explanation: Sirius gives Harry a two-way mirror for emergency communication, but Harry forgets about it until after Sirius's death.

questions.question_text: What happens to the shelved Time-Turners in the Ministry's Time Room during the battle in the Department of Mysteries?
questions.correct_answer: They are smashed and destroyed in the fighting
distractors: They are stolen by Death Eaters
They are confiscated safely by the Order
They multiply time itself, trapping the combatants
questions.explanation: The destruction of the Ministry's stock of Time-Turners during the melee has lasting consequences for later books.

questions.question_text: What does Voldemort do the instant he realizes Dumbledore has arrived at the Ministry Atrium to confront him?
questions.correct_answer: He abandons the fight and flees
distractors: He turns his wand on Harry immediately
questions.explanation: Even Voldemort chooses to escape rather than face Dumbledore directly once he arrives.

questions.question_text: What is a bezoar primarily used to treat?
questions.explanation: A bezoar, a stone from a goat's stomach, can save a person from most poisons.

questions.question_text: What does Veritaserum force a person who drinks it to do?
questions.explanation: Veritaserum is a powerful truth potion that compels the drinker to answer honestly.

questions.question_text: What state does the Draught of Living Death put its drinker into?
questions.explanation: The Draught of Living Death is one of the most powerful sleeping potions known to wizardkind.

questions.question_text: In his first-class speech, Snape boasts he can teach students to bottle fame, brew glory, and even put a stopper in what?
questions.explanation: Snape's dramatic opening speech to his first-year Potions class ends with this famous line, delivered in both the book and film.

questions.question_text: According to Snape, his Potions class involves little of what, unlike other subjects at Hogwarts?
questions.explanation: Snape tells his first-years that Potions requires precision, not the wand-waving of other classes.

questions.question_text: What color is Felix Felicis, the potion also known as Liquid Luck?
questions.explanation: Felix Felicis is a shimmering, molten-gold potion.

questions.question_text: What mistake causes Neville's cauldron to collapse in Harry's very first Potions lesson?
questions.correct_answer: He adds porcupine quills before removing the cauldron from the fire
distractors: He uses the wrong number of snake fangs
He forgets to crush the ingredients first
He lets the potion boil for too long
questions.explanation: Snape's instructions require the cauldron off the heat before adding porcupine quills; Neville skips this step and his potion eats through his cauldron.

questions.question_text: What does the smell of Amortentia reveal about the person smelling it?
questions.correct_answer: The things that attract them most
questions.explanation: Amortentia smells different to each person, according to what they find most attractive.

questions.question_text: What does Devil's Snare do to anyone who struggles against it?
distractors: Sprays them with a foul-smelling liquid
questions.explanation: Devil's Snare is a plant that constricts around anyone who thrashes against it, making the grip worse the more they fight.

questions.question_text: What does a young Mandrake root look like when pulled from its pot?
questions.explanation: Mandrakes resemble human babies when young, and mature into more human-like, screaming plants.

questions.question_text: Which Hogwarts house does Herbology teacher Pomona Sprout belong to?
questions.explanation: Professor Sprout is Head of Hufflepuff House as well as the Herbology teacher.

questions.question_text: Which Hogwarts house is Potions master Severus Snape the Head of?
questions.explanation: Snape serves as Head of Slytherin House for most of the series.

questions.question_text: In which part of Hogwarts castle are Potions lessons traditionally held?
questions.explanation: Potions classes take place in cold, dimly lit dungeon classrooms.

questions.question_text: What material must the scales on a first-year's Hogwarts supply list be made of?
questions.explanation: Harry's Hogwarts letter specifies a set of brass scales among the required equipment.

questions.question_text: Besides a cauldron, what glass equipment does the first-year supply list require for Potions?
questions.correct_answer: A set of glass or crystal phials
questions.explanation: Phials are used to bottle and store finished potions.

questions.question_text: What kind of protective gloves does the Hogwarts first-year supply list recommend?
questions.explanation: Protective gloves guard students' hands from dangerous ingredients and plants.

questions.question_text: What metal are standard Hogwarts cauldrons, like the one on Harry's first-year list, made of?
questions.explanation: Harry's supply list calls for a standard size two pewter cauldron.

questions.question_text: What happens if raw, unprocessed Bubotuber pus touches bare skin?
distractors: It has no effect at all
questions.explanation: Bubotuber pus is dangerous in its raw form and must be handled with gloves, even though bottled versions treat acne.

questions.question_text: What does Polyjuice Potion look like while it is brewing, according to Hermione?
questions.explanation: Hermione's cauldron of Polyjuice Potion is described as an unappetizing, thick, dark sludge before it is ready.

questions.question_text: About how long does it take for Skele-Gro to regrow a set of bones, according to Madam Pomfrey?
questions.explanation: Madam Pomfrey warns Harry that regrowing bones with Skele-Gro is a slow, painful process that takes through the night.

questions.question_text: In which book is the Wolfsbane Potion first introduced to readers?
questions.explanation: The Wolfsbane Potion, brewed for Lupin, is introduced in Prisoner of Azkaban.

questions.question_text: Which powdered animal horn appears on Harry's first-year list of potion ingredients to buy?
questions.explanation: Powdered unicorn horn is among the standard ingredients first-years must purchase.

questions.question_text: Which dried plant is a listed ingredient in the simple Cure for Boils potion Harry's class first brews?
questions.explanation: Dried nettles are one of the ingredients in the basic Cure for Boils.

questions.question_text: Which stewed ingredient goes into the Cure for Boils potion?
questions.explanation: Stewed horned slugs are part of the recipe for the Cure for Boils.

questions.question_text: How many snake fangs does the Cure for Boils recipe call for?
questions.explanation: Snape's instructions for the Cure for Boils specify six snake fangs.

questions.question_text: Which house does Gryffindor share Potions lessons with in Harry's early years?
distractors: None; they have no shared classes
questions.explanation: Gryffindor and Slytherin famously share Potions lessons, fueling their rivalry.

questions.question_text: What remarkable healing property do phoenix tears have?
questions.correct_answer: They can heal almost any wound
questions.explanation: Phoenix tears possess powerful healing properties, as Fawkes demonstrates on Harry.

questions.question_text: What must a person do to survive after drinking unicorn blood, according to Firenze?
questions.correct_answer: Live a cursed half-life from the moment it touches their lips
distractors: Drink a bezoar potion within a day
questions.explanation: Firenze explains that drinking unicorn blood keeps you alive but at the price of a cursed existence.

questions.question_text: Which violent magical tree on the Hogwarts grounds attacks anyone who gets too close?
questions.explanation: The Whomping Willow lashes out at anything that comes within reach of its branches.

questions.question_text: What does the Whomping Willow conceal at its roots?
questions.correct_answer: A secret passage to the Shrieking Shack
distractors: An entrance to the Chamber of Secrets
questions.explanation: The tree was planted to hide the tunnel Lupin used to reach the Shrieking Shack during his transformations.

questions.question_text: How is Gillyweed generally described in appearance?
questions.correct_answer: Slimy and grey-green, like rubbery rat tails
questions.explanation: Gillyweed's slimy, rubbery appearance belies its usefulness for underwater breathing.

questions.question_text: What vessel do Hogwarts students typically brew their potions in?
questions.explanation: Cauldrons are the standard brewing vessel used in every Potions class.

questions.question_text: What tool do students use to crush and grind solid potion ingredients?
questions.explanation: A mortar and pestle is standard Potions equipment for preparing ingredients.

questions.question_text: What commonly lines the shelves of Snape's dungeon classroom and office?
questions.correct_answer: Jars of pickled or preserved specimens
questions.explanation: Snape's dungeon is famously described as lined with jars containing slimy, preserved ingredients.

questions.question_text: Who wrote 'One Thousand Magical Herbs and Fungi,' the standard first-year Herbology textbook?
questions.explanation: Phyllida Spore is credited as the author of the first-year Herbology textbook.

questions.question_text: Who wrote 'Magical Drafts and Potions,' the standard first-year Potions textbook?
questions.explanation: Arsenius Jigger is the credited author of the first-year Potions textbook.

questions.question_text: Which Hogwarts matron treats students for potion-related injuries in the hospital wing?
questions.explanation: Poppy Pomfrey is the school nurse who treats mishaps from Potions and Herbology classes alike.

questions.question_text: What kind of pet does Neville Longbottom own that suffers several magical mishaps over the years?
questions.explanation: Neville's toad, Trevor, is repeatedly caught up in classroom accidents.

questions.question_text: What is Herbology primarily the study of?
questions.explanation: Herbology is the Hogwarts subject devoted to magical plants and fungi.

questions.question_text: In what type of structure are Herbology lessons typically held at Hogwarts?
questions.explanation: Herbology classes take place in the greenhouses on the Hogwarts grounds.

questions.question_text: What sarcastic title does Snape use for Harry during roll call in his very first Potions class?
questions.explanation: Snape mocks Harry's fame by calling him 'our new celebrity' when taking attendance.

questions.question_text: What does Hagrid use to fertilize his giant pumpkins for the Halloween feast?
questions.explanation: Hagrid relies on dragon dung as fertilizer to grow his prize-winning pumpkins.

questions.question_text: Which Weasley twins' invention causes the eater to develop a convincing nosebleed, letting them skip class?
questions.explanation: Nosebleed Nougat is part of Fred and George's Skiving Snackbox line, designed to fake an excuse to leave class.

questions.question_text: In which subject does Neville Longbottom excel far more than in Potions?
questions.explanation: Despite struggling in Potions, Neville shows real talent and knowledge in Herbology.

questions.question_text: Which member of the trio first realizes the plant trapping them below the trapdoor is Devil's Snare?
questions.explanation: Hermione recognizes the plant from her Herbology studies and knows to relax rather than struggle.

questions.question_text: What does a shop sign in Diagon Alley advertise the price of, per ounce, catching Harry's eye?
questions.explanation: Wandering through Diagon Alley, Harry notices a sign listing the price of dragon liver by the ounce.

questions.question_text: What do the Latin roots of 'Felix Felicis' roughly translate to?
questions.explanation: 'Felix' is Latin for lucky or happy, fitting the potion's effect of extraordinary good luck.

questions.question_text: What physically happens to Fred and George after drinking their homemade Aging Potion?
questions.explanation: Their attempt to cross Dumbledore's Age Line with an Aging Potion leaves them with long white beards instead of fooling the spell.

questions.question_text: What is notably true of Flobberworms, whose mucus is sometimes used as a potion ingredient?
questions.correct_answer: They are famously among the dullest, least active magical creatures
distractors: They are highly venomous and aggressive
They glow faintly in the dark
questions.explanation: Flobberworms are known for being sluggish, barely-moving creatures, in contrast to their occasional use as a potion ingredient.

questions.question_text: Which professor is Head of Gryffindor House, the house that shares Potions lessons with Slytherin?
questions.explanation: McGonagall is Head of Gryffindor House throughout most of the series.

questions.question_text: What Herbology-related notes does Hermione recall to correctly identify Devil's Snare in Philosopher's Stone?
questions.correct_answer: Her class notes on the plant from Herbology lessons
distractors: A page torn from Snape's Potions textbook
A warning label on a greenhouse door
Hagrid's offhand comment about the plant
questions.explanation: Hermione's knowledge from Herbology lessons lets her recognize Devil's Snare and know how to escape it.

questions.question_text: How is Snape's dungeon classroom typically described in terms of atmosphere?
questions.explanation: The Potions classroom is set in the dungeons, giving it a famously cold and gloomy atmosphere.

questions.question_text: Which ingredient, along with leeches and daisy roots, appears in the Shrinking Solution recipe taught in a second-year Potions class?
questions.explanation: The Shrinking Solution recipe includes shrivelfig, leeches, rat spleen, and daisy roots among its ingredients.

questions.question_text: Which root is a listed ingredient in the Shrinking Solution, alongside shrivelfig and leeches?
questions.explanation: Daisy roots are part of the Shrinking Solution recipe used in a second-year Potions class.

questions.question_text: Which Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes Skiving Snackbox item causes the eater to develop a convincing fake fever?
questions.explanation: Fever Fudge is one of Fred and George's Skiving Snackbox items, designed to fake illness convincingly.

questions.question_text: Which of these is also a required ingredient in Hermione's Polyjuice Potion recipe, besides boomslang skin and lacewing flies?
questions.explanation: Knotgrass is one of the several ingredients Hermione's Polyjuice recipe calls for.

questions.question_text: Which slimy bloodsucking creature is a listed ingredient in the Polyjuice Potion recipe?
questions.explanation: Leeches appear among the several ingredients required for Polyjuice Potion.

questions.question_text: What powdered animal horn does the Polyjuice Potion recipe call for?
questions.explanation: Hermione's Polyjuice recipe includes powdered bicorn horn among its ingredients.

questions.question_text: What property of Basilisk venom makes it valuable beyond being a deadly poison?
questions.correct_answer: It is one of the few known substances that can destroy a Horcrux
distractors: It can cure any potion gone wrong
questions.explanation: Basilisk venom is established as one of the rare substances able to destroy a Horcrux, as Harry uses it on the diary.

questions.question_text: Which potion, listed in the contents of the textbook Advanced Potion-Making, is meant to keep the drinker awake and alert?
questions.explanation: The Wideye Potion appears among the potions listed in Harry's sixth-year textbook.

questions.question_text: What is the general purpose of a Girding Potion, one of the potions listed in Advanced Potion-Making?
questions.correct_answer: To fortify or brace the drinker, often before a difficult task
distractors: To induce a deep, dreamless sleep
To reverse the effects of aging
questions.explanation: The Girding Potion is understood to be a bracing, fortifying potion listed among the NEWT-level potions in Harry's textbook.

questions.question_text: Which of these potion names genuinely appears in the table of contents of the NEWT-level textbook Advanced Potion-Making?
questions.explanation: Hiccoughing Solution is one of the real potions listed in Harry's sixth-year Potions textbook.

questions.question_text: Which of these potion names genuinely appears alongside Elixir to Induce Euphoria in Advanced Potion-Making's table of contents?
questions.explanation: The Babbling Beverage is listed among the potions in Harry's sixth-year textbook.

questions.question_text: Besides its unique smell, what visual features identify Amortentia in Slughorn's classroom demonstration?
questions.correct_answer: A mother-of-pearl sheen and steam rising in distinctive spirals
distractors: A bubbling black surface with green sparks
A rainbow shimmer that changes with the weather
questions.explanation: Slughorn's demonstration cauldron of Amortentia is described with a mother-of-pearl sheen and spiraling steam.

questions.question_text: Why is Felix Felicis banned from official competitions like Quidditch matches, according to Slughorn?
questions.correct_answer: It gives the user an unfair advantage through extraordinary good luck
distractors: It is classified as a dangerous poison
It is prohibitively expensive to brew for players
questions.explanation: Slughorn explains that Felix Felicis would give an unfair edge in any competition, so its use is banned.

questions.question_text: What does Slughorn warn Amortentia can never actually create in a person?
questions.explanation: Slughorn stresses that Amortentia only creates powerful infatuation or obsession, never genuine love.

questions.question_text: Which oddly named plant, grown by Neville in advanced Herbology, must be pruned while wearing earmuffs because it screeches when cut?
questions.explanation: Screechsnaps are a Herbology plant Neville tends that shriek loudly when pruned.

questions.question_text: In what kind of environment does Devil's Snare thrive, making light and warmth its natural enemy?
questions.explanation: Devil's Snare flourishes in dark and damp places, which is why light and heat cause it to retreat.

questions.question_text: Which distinctive candied treat does Professor Slughorn love serving to guests at his gatherings?
questions.explanation: Slughorn is fond of offering crystallized pineapple to those he hopes to charm.

questions.question_text: Why does Slughorn attend Aragog the giant spider's funeral in Half-Blood Prince?
questions.correct_answer: To secretly collect Aragog's valuable venom for Potions ingredients
distractors: To pay his respects as an old friend of Hagrid's
To confirm Aragog is truly dead for the Ministry
To retrieve a hidden ingredient Aragog guarded
questions.explanation: Slughorn's real motive for attending the funeral is to collect the giant spider's venom, a rare and valuable Potions ingredient.

questions.question_text: Why does Snape imply the Wolfsbane Potion is unusually difficult to brew correctly?
questions.correct_answer: Its recipe is extremely complex, and few wizards can manage it
distractors: It requires ingredients that no longer exist
It must be brewed only during a solar eclipse
It is illegal to brew outside St Mungo's
questions.explanation: Snape's grudging effort to brew Wolfsbane monthly reflects how complex and demanding the potion is to get right.

questions.question_text: What is notably true about bezoars, despite Snape's simple description of where to find one?
questions.correct_answer: Not every goat has one, making them somewhat rare to come by
distractors: They can only be harvested from a dead goat
They lose potency after a single use
They must be enchanted before use
questions.explanation: While bezoars are found in goats' stomachs, not every goat produces one, so they aren't always easy to obtain.

questions.question_text: What is the only known cure demonstrated in the books for Basilisk venom poisoning?
questions.explanation: Fawkes's tears save Harry's life after he is bitten by the Basilisk's fang in the Chamber of Secrets.

questions.question_text: Based on its name and classroom context, what is a Confusing Concoction generally understood to cause in the drinker?
questions.explanation: A Confusing Concoction is understood, by name, to leave the drinker disoriented and confused.

questions.question_text: Which mineral, associated with lunar magic, is a listed ingredient in the Draught of Peace?
questions.explanation: Powdered moonstone is one of the ingredients called for in the Draught of Peace recipe.

questions.question_text: Which herb, also known as a real-world sleep aid, is an ingredient in the Draught of Peace?
questions.explanation: Sprigs of valerian are part of the Draught of Peace recipe used in the O.W.L. Potions exam.

questions.question_text: About how often must Lupin drink the Wolfsbane Potion in the days leading up to the full moon?
questions.correct_answer: Once a day for about a week beforehand
distractors: Only once, the morning of the full moon
Every hour throughout the entire month
Once at the start of each school term
questions.explanation: Wolfsbane Potion must be taken regularly, roughly daily, in the run-up to the full moon to be effective.

questions.question_text: What is different about the danger posed by a fully mature Mandrake's cry compared to a young Mandrake's?
questions.correct_answer: A mature Mandrake's cry is fatal, while a young one's merely knocks a listener unconscious
distractors: A mature Mandrake's cry causes deafness, while a young one's causes blindness
A mature Mandrake's cry is silent, while only young ones scream
There is no difference; both are equally harmless
questions.explanation: Mandrakes become more dangerous as they mature: a young one's cry can knock you out, but a mature one's cry can kill.

questions.question_text: What is the primary danger of getting too close to a mature Venomous Tentacula?
questions.correct_answer: Its thrashing, fanged vines can bite and whip at you
distractors: It releases a cloud of toxic spores
It secretes an invisible, odorless poison
questions.explanation: Venomous Tentacula is an aggressive plant whose vines can snap and bite anyone who ventures too close.
questions.source_ref: Order of the Phoenix / Half-Blood Prince

questions.question_text: Besides a hair from each target, what else must Harry and Ron obtain to convincingly impersonate Crabbe and Goyle using Polyjuice Potion?
questions.correct_answer: Clothing similar in size to Crabbe's and Goyle's own
distractors: A second dose of Polyjuice for emergencies
A separate potion to disguise their voices
questions.explanation: Polyjuice Potion transforms the body but not clothing, so Harry and Ron need robes that actually fit their new forms.

questions.question_text: Which Potions professor taught Harry's mother, Lily Evans, decades before teaching Harry himself?
questions.explanation: Slughorn taught Potions during the Marauders' era and fondly remembers Lily Evans as a talented student.

questions.question_text: About how long does Snape say it took him to brew the Veritaserum used to interrogate Barty Crouch Jr.?
questions.explanation: Snape mentions the lengthy, careful brewing process behind the Veritaserum used at the end of Goblet of Fire.

questions.question_text: What happens to a student under the effects of an overdose of the Elixir to Induce Euphoria, as shown in Slughorn's class?
questions.correct_answer: They become giddy, overconfident, and prone to singing
distractors: They fall into a coma-like sleep
They lose all memory of the last hour
questions.explanation: Slughorn's classroom demonstration shows a volunteer growing giddy and overconfident from too much Elixir to Induce Euphoria.

questions.question_text: Across Harry's seven years at Hogwarts, which two professors teach him Potions?
distractors: Severus Snape only, for all seven years
questions.explanation: Snape teaches Potions through Harry's fifth year before Slughorn takes over in year six.

questions.question_text: According to Snape's instructions, at what stage must porcupine quills be added to a Cure for Boils potion?
questions.correct_answer: Only after the cauldron has been removed from the fire
distractors: At the very start, before any heat is applied
Exactly halfway through the brewing time
Only once the potion turns purple
questions.explanation: Adding porcupine quills while the potion is still over the flame causes a dangerous reaction, as Neville discovers.

questions.question_text: In Potions terms, what does a 'sopophorous bean' do to those who consume the potion it's brewed into?
questions.explanation: Sopophorous beans are a key sleep-inducing ingredient in potions like the Draught of Living Death.

questions.question_text: What diversion helps Hermione slip into Snape's office to steal ingredients for the Polyjuice Potion?
questions.correct_answer: A commotion caused elsewhere in the corridor to distract Snape and Filch
distractors: A fake fire alarm set off by Peeves
An owl delivery mix-up in the Great Hall
questions.explanation: The trio arranges a distraction so Hermione can sneak into Snape's private stores unnoticed.

questions.question_text: Which of these potions is Snape never actually shown or described brewing at any point in the series?
distractors: The Cure for Boils demonstration potion
questions.explanation: Felix Felicis is strongly associated with Slughorn, while Snape is shown brewing Wolfsbane and Veritaserum.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum O.W.L. grade Slughorn accepts for entry into his N.E.W.T.-level Potions class, one level below Snape's old requirement?
questions.explanation: Slughorn relaxes Snape's stricter 'Outstanding required' rule, allowing students with Exceeds Expectations to continue Potions.

questions.question_text: Which magical creature saves Harry's life with its tears after he is bitten by the Basilisk in the Chamber of Secrets?
questions.explanation: Fawkes's healing tears cure Harry of the fatal Basilisk venom.

questions.question_text: Which Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes product causes the eater to faint convincingly, useful for skipping an unwanted class?
questions.explanation: Fainting Fancies are part of the Skiving Snackbox line meant to fake illness.

questions.question_text: Where does Harry hide the Half-Blood Prince's book after the Sectumsempra incident with Draco?
distractors: Under a loose floorboard in his dormitory
The Restricted Section of the library
questions.explanation: Fearing punishment, Harry hides the Prince's book among countless other objects in the Room of Requirement.

questions.question_text: Relying on the Half-Blood Prince's annotated textbook, what changes for Harry in Potions class for the first time?
questions.correct_answer: He consistently outperforms Hermione at brewing potions
distractors: He is finally allowed to sit with Slughorn's favorites
He no longer needs a cauldron at all
He is exempted from the final Potions exam
questions.explanation: With the Prince's shortcuts and tips, Harry surprises everyone, including Hermione, by excelling at Potions.

questions.question_text: Why is Snape especially eager to reclaim his old textbook once he suspects Harry has been using it?
questions.correct_answer: It contains spells and secrets he wrote as a student that he doesn't want discovered
distractors: It has his home address written inside the cover
It lists his real feelings about other professors
It contains a map to his private chambers
questions.explanation: The book reveals Snape's own school-era inventions and nickname, which he'd rather keep hidden.

questions.question_text: Which animal organ, alongside shrivelfig and daisy roots, is an ingredient in the Shrinking Solution recipe?
questions.explanation: Rat spleen is one of the ingredients listed for the Shrinking Solution taught in a second-year Potions class.

questions.question_text: What does Slughorn proudly display in his office and train compartment, showing off his connections to famous former students?
questions.correct_answer: Photographs and mementos of well-known former pupils
questions.explanation: Slughorn keeps souvenirs of his most famous or promising former students as a point of pride.

questions.question_text: According to Golpalott's Third Law, taught in Harry's sixth-year Potions class, what must the antidote for a blended poison be, relative to the antidotes for its individual components?
questions.correct_answer: Greater than the mere sum of the antidotes for each separate component
distractors: Exactly equal to the sum of the individual antidotes
Weaker than any single component's antidote
Identical regardless of how many poisons are blended
questions.explanation: Golpalott's Third Law states that a blended poison's antidote is more than simply the sum of the antidotes to each ingredient poison.

questions.question_text: In Slughorn's class, what surprisingly simple answer does Harry give, learned from the Prince's notes, when asked to formulate an antidote for common poisons?
questions.correct_answer: He simply writes 'Just add a bezoar.'
distractors: He brews a complete antidote from scratch
He cites Veritaserum as a universal cure
He recommends immediate use of Skele-Gro
questions.explanation: Rather than doing the complex work Golpalott's Law implies, Harry uses the Prince's shortcut and just notes that a bezoar will do the job.

questions.question_text: Not counting the piece of the person being copied, how many other ingredients does Hermione's Polyjuice Potion recipe require?
questions.explanation: Hermione's recipe calls for lacewing flies, leeches, powdered bicorn horn, knotgrass, fluxweed, and boomslang skin, plus a bit of the person.

questions.question_text: How many different common names does Snape use for the very same plant in his first Potions lesson?
distractors: One; he only ever uses a single name
questions.explanation: Snape's opening riddle reveals that aconite, monkshood, and wolfsbane are all names for one and the same plant.

questions.question_text: Which part of a unicorn is used as a standard Potions ingredient, rather than as a wand core?
questions.explanation: Unicorn hair is famously a wand core, while powdered unicorn horn is the part used in potion-making.

questions.question_text: What is the actual in-universe name given to the potion guarding the fake locket Horcrux that Dumbledore is forced to drink in the cave?
questions.correct_answer: It is never given a name in the books
questions.explanation: The potion protecting the Horcrux in the cave is described in detail but is never actually named in the text.

questions.question_text: What cruel enchantment on the potion in the cave forces Dumbledore to keep drinking despite his obvious suffering?
questions.correct_answer: The basin magically refills itself unless it is completely emptied
distractors: It can only be drunk once every hour
It must be drunk in complete silence
It repels any attempt to stop drinking early
questions.explanation: The basin cannot simply be scooped from; it refills itself, forcing the drinker to empty it entirely before it can be removed.

questions.question_text: What does drinking the potion in the cave force Dumbledore to experience?
questions.correct_answer: Overwhelming thirst alongside apparent hallucinations that torment him
distractors: Total memory loss of the last decade
Instant physical paralysis with no visions
questions.explanation: The potion causes Dumbledore visible agony, thirst, and what appear to be tormenting visions as he drinks it.

questions.question_text: In the potion used to resurrect Voldemort, how is the 'bone of the father' ingredient obtained?
questions.correct_answer: Unknowingly given, taken from his father's grave
distractors: Willingly given by a living relative
questions.explanation: The incantation specifies the bone of the father be 'unknowingly given'; it is dust taken from Tom Riddle Sr.'s grave.

questions.question_text: In the potion used to resurrect Voldemort, how is the 'flesh of the servant' ingredient described in the incantation?
questions.correct_answer: Willingly given, as Wormtail cuts off his own hand
distractors: Unknowingly given, taken while he slept
questions.explanation: Wormtail willingly sacrifices his own hand to provide 'flesh of the servant, willingly given.'

questions.question_text: In the potion used to resurrect Voldemort, how must the 'blood of the enemy' be obtained, according to the incantation?
distractors: Drawn from a defeated enemy's corpse
questions.explanation: Unlike the other two ingredients, Harry's blood specifically must be forcibly taken, a detail Wormtail is careful to follow.

questions.question_text: What does Dumbledore believe Merope Gaunt used to make Tom Riddle Sr. fall in love with her, before she stopped using it?
questions.explanation: Dumbledore suggests Merope kept Tom Riddle Sr. under the influence of a love potion until she chose to stop, at which point he abandoned her.

questions.question_text: In Half-Blood Prince, what happens to Ron after he eats Chocolate Cauldrons that were actually meant for Harry?
questions.correct_answer: He falls under a love potion's spell and becomes obsessed with Romilda Vane
distractors: He is poisoned and nearly dies immediately
He develops a severe allergic rash
questions.explanation: The spiked chocolates were intended for Harry, but Ron eats them instead and becomes infatuated with Romilda Vane.

questions.question_text: What does Slughorn give Ron to counteract the love potion's effects, just before the poisoned mead incident?
questions.correct_answer: An antidote he has on hand
distractors: Nothing; the effects wear off naturally
questions.explanation: Slughorn treats Ron with a readily available antidote to snap him out of his love-potion-induced obsession.

questions.question_text: Besides brewing shortcuts, what dangerous invention does the Half-Blood Prince's annotated Potions book also contain?
distractors: A recipe for an untraceable poison
questions.explanation: Snape's old textbook holds more than potion tips; it also contains his own invented curse, Sectumsempra.

questions.question_text: Before an important Quidditch match, what does Harry pretend to do to Ron's drink to boost his confidence?
questions.correct_answer: Pretend to slip him a dose of Felix Felicis, without actually doing so
distractors: Actually dose him with real Felix Felicis
questions.explanation: Harry lets Ron believe he's been given Liquid Luck, when in fact Ron drinks nothing but ordinary juice.

questions.question_text: According to Slughorn, roughly how long does it take to brew Felix Felicis correctly?
questions.explanation: Slughorn notes that properly brewing Felix Felicis is a long, complicated process taking around half a year.

questions.question_text: How does Barty Crouch Jr. maintain his Polyjuice-based disguise as Mad-Eye Moody for nearly an entire school year?
questions.correct_answer: By regularly redosing from a hip flask he carries at all times
distractors: By brewing an entirely new batch every morning
By using a single dose that lasts the whole year
By relying on a permanent Transfiguration instead
questions.explanation: Crouch Jr. keeps Polyjuice Potion in a hip flask and sips from it frequently to sustain the disguise.

questions.question_text: Is the unnamed potion guarding the cave Horcrux the same potion as the Draught of Living Death?
questions.correct_answer: No, they are two entirely different, unrelated potions
distractors: Yes, they are the exact same potion
The cave potion is a stronger version of it
The cave potion is the antidote to it
questions.explanation: Despite both being dangerous, dramatic potions involving sleep-like or tormenting effects, the cave potion and the Draught of Living Death are never identified as the same brew.

questions.question_text: What is unique about the two colored halves of a single Puking Pastille?
questions.correct_answer: One end induces vomiting, and the other end reverses it
distractors: Each half causes a different color of vomit
One half is a decoy with no effect at all
Eating both halves together cancels any reaction
questions.explanation: A Puking Pastille is designed so eating one colored end makes you sick, and the other end lets you recover convincingly.

questions.question_text: According to Neville, where does his rare plant Mimbulus Mimbletonia originate?
questions.explanation: Neville proudly explains that his great-uncle Algie's gift, Mimbulus Mimbletonia, comes from Assyria.

questions.question_text: What general Potions principle does the Half-Blood Prince's note about sopophorous beans illustrate?
questions.correct_answer: That how an ingredient is physically prepared can drastically change a potion's potency
distractors: That more ingredients always make a stronger potion
That stirring direction never actually matters
That only fresh ingredients can be used in any potion
questions.explanation: The Prince's trick of crushing rather than cutting the bean shows that preparation method, not just ingredients, shapes a potion's outcome.

questions.question_text: How is the freshly brewed Wolfsbane Potion typically described when Snape delivers it to Lupin's office?
questions.correct_answer: Steaming or smoking in its container
questions.explanation: The Wolfsbane Potion Snape brings to Lupin is often described as visibly smoking.

questions.question_text: What do the roots of the word 'Veritaserum' literally combine to mean?
questions.explanation: 'Veritaserum' combines Latin-derived roots for truth ('veritas') and a liquid or serum, fitting its function as a truth potion.

questions.question_text: In which specific school year does Horace Slughorn take over teaching Potions from Severus Snape?
questions.explanation: Slughorn arrives to teach Potions the same year Snape finally becomes the Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher.

questions.question_text: Whose old school textbook, once belonging to a future Death Eater's teenage self, does Harry rely on throughout sixth-year Potions?
questions.correct_answer: Severus Snape's, under his old nickname 'the Half-Blood Prince'
questions.explanation: The battered, annotated textbook Harry uses once belonged to a young Severus Snape.

questions.question_text: Which single item, described as findable 'in a goat's stomach' in Harry's very first Potions lesson, later saves Ron Weasley's life?
questions.explanation: The very antidote Snape describes to first-year Harry is the one Harry later uses to save Ron from poisoned mead.

questions.question_text: What happens to Voldemort's body immediately after the rebirth potion is completed in the graveyard?
questions.correct_answer: He rises from the cauldron restored to his own body, fully formed
distractors: He remains a spectral, bodiless form
He appears as an infant needing further care
He collapses and must be revived separately
questions.explanation: Once the potion is complete, Voldemort emerges from the cauldron in his own physical body once more.

questions.question_text: Which fast-acting healing herb, mentioned in Harry's earliest Potions lessons, does Hermione carry with her and use to treat Ron's near-fatal snake bite years later?
questions.explanation: Dittany's healing properties, established early on, prove crucial when Hermione uses it to close Ron's wound in Deathly Hallows.

questions.question_text: Which O.W.L.-level potion, meant to calm the drinker, shares a 'dangerous sleep' theme with the far more infamous Draught of Living Death if brewed incorrectly?
questions.explanation: A mistake while brewing the Draught of Peace can send the drinker into a deep, dangerous sleep, echoing the far deadlier Draught of Living Death.

questions.question_text: Which two ingredients, combined per Snape's very first classroom riddle, create the same potion Harry later perfects using the Prince's crushed-bean trick?
questions.explanation: Asphodel and wormwood together form the Draught of Living Death, the very potion Harry improves years later with the Prince's technique.

questions.question_text: What does Hermione's cat-hair mishap with Polyjuice Potion demonstrate about the potion's limits?
questions.correct_answer: It cannot be used to transform a human into a non-human creature
distractors: It only works on witches, not wizards
It requires the hair of a magical creature to work at all
It can only be brewed successfully by skilled adults
questions.explanation: Hermione's accidental use of cat hair, leaving her partially feline, shows Polyjuice Potion isn't meant for human-to-animal transformation.

questions.question_text: What must be true of the Mandrakes used to brew the Restorative Draught in Chamber of Secrets?
questions.correct_answer: They must be fully mature before the draught can be brewed
distractors: They must be grown entirely underwater
They must be harvested at midnight only
They must be grown from imported seeds
questions.explanation: The petrified victims must wait for the school's Mandrakes to reach maturity before the cure can be brewed.

questions.question_text: Which professor is responsible for tending and repotting the maturing Mandrakes needed to cure the petrified victims in Chamber of Secrets?
questions.explanation: As the Herbology teacher, Professor Sprout oversees the Mandrakes as they grow toward maturity.

questions.question_text: How is the surface of Neville's plant, Mimbulus Mimbletonia, typically described?
questions.correct_answer: Covered in throbbing, boil-like green swellings
questions.explanation: Mimbulus Mimbletonia's odd, pulsating, boil-covered surface is part of what makes it such an unusual plant.

questions.question_text: According to Hermione's Polyjuice Potion recipe, how must the boomslang skin specifically be prepared?
questions.explanation: Hermione's notes call specifically for shredded boomslang skin, one of the ingredients she steals from Snape's stores.

questions.question_text: At what stage of brewing must the unique 'piece of the person' ingredient be added to Polyjuice Potion?
questions.correct_answer: Only after the six base ingredients have finished stewing
distractors: Before any other ingredient is added
Exactly halfway through the month-long process
At the same time as the boomslang skin
questions.explanation: The personal ingredient, such as a hair, is added once the base potion made from the other six ingredients is otherwise complete.

questions.question_text: In Deathly Hallows, whose hair is used to create six Polyjuice decoys to help the real Harry escape the Dursleys' house safely?
questions.explanation: Members of the Order use Polyjuice Potion made with Harry's own hair to create decoys for the dangerous journey away from Privet Drive.

questions.question_text: How many 'Potters,' including the real Harry, set out from Privet Drive during the escape plan in Deathly Hallows?
questions.explanation: The plan uses six Polyjuice decoys alongside the real Harry, making seven Potters in total.

questions.question_text: Roughly how long does each decoy's Polyjuice disguise last during the Seven Potters escape before needing to be redosed?
distractors: The entire night without wearing off
questions.explanation: Like all Polyjuice Potion, the decoys' disguises only last around an hour before needing to be renewed.

questions.question_text: How does Barty Crouch Jr. sustain his Polyjuice disguise as Mad-Eye Moody for so long, using the real Moody as a source?
questions.correct_answer: By periodically taking hair and other samples from the imprisoned real Moody
distractors: By using a single permanent dose that never wears off
By relying on Moody's own wand instead of the potion
By having Moody brew fresh potion for him each week
questions.explanation: The real Moody, kept alive but imprisoned in his own trunk, unwillingly supplies the materials needed to keep Crouch Jr.'s disguise going.

questions.question_text: How do Harry and Ron typically react to the taste of Polyjuice Potion when transforming into Crabbe and Goyle?
questions.correct_answer: They find it disgusting and vile
distractors: They feel no taste at all
questions.explanation: Polyjuice Potion is notoriously unpleasant to drink, and Harry and Ron are visibly disgusted by it.

questions.question_text: What does Slughorn keep in a small crystal flagon at the front of his very first NEWT Potions class, separate from the cauldrons students brew in?
questions.correct_answer: A prepared sample of Felix Felicis, offered as a class prize
distractors: A vial of Veritaserum for demonstration only
A dose of Amortentia for identification practice
An antidote sample for Golpalott's Law lessons
questions.explanation: Slughorn displays a small golden vial of Felix Felicis as the prize for whoever brews the best potion that lesson.

questions.question_text: According to the books, is a reliable antidote to Veritaserum ever described?
questions.correct_answer: No, none is ever mentioned in the books
distractors: Yes, a bezoar reliably works against it
Yes, powdered moonstone reverses its effects
Yes, but only Dumbledore knows the recipe
questions.explanation: Despite Veritaserum's prominence, canon never describes a working antidote to it.

questions.question_text: What do the Girding Potion, Wideye Potion, Hiccoughing Solution, and Babbling Beverage all have in common?
questions.correct_answer: They are all listed in the table of contents of Advanced Potion-Making, Harry's sixth-year textbook
distractors: They are all illegal to brew without a Ministry license
They are all invented by the Half-Blood Prince himself
They are all specifically banned from Hogwarts grounds
questions.explanation: All four are genuine potions named in the contents of the NEWT-level textbook Harry uses in Half-Blood Prince.

questions.question_text: Which single sixth-year textbook connects Harry's superior Draught of Living Death, his bezoar shortcut answer, and the invented curse Sectumsempra?
questions.correct_answer: Advanced Potion-Making, the Half-Blood Prince's annotated copy
distractors: One Thousand Magical Herbs and Fungi
questions.explanation: All three stem from the same annotated textbook Harry uses throughout Half-Blood Prince.

questions.question_text: Which single Potions teacher's fondness for crystallized pineapple and for collecting rare ingredients like Aragog's venom defines his personality?
questions.explanation: Slughorn's love of fine treats and rare, prestigious ingredients are hallmarks of his character throughout Half-Blood Prince.

questions.question_text: Which single potion's recipe requires fluxweed picked during a full moon and lacewing flies stewed for twenty-one days?
questions.explanation: Both the full-moon fluxweed and the twenty-one-day lacewing fly requirement belong to the same recipe: Polyjuice Potion.

questions.question_text: Which single, unnamed potion features a self-refilling basin and leaves Dumbledore tormented by thirst and visions?
questions.correct_answer: The potion guarding the Horcrux locket in the cave
distractors: The rebirth potion from Goblet of Fire
questions.explanation: These details all describe the same dangerous, unnamed potion Dumbledore is forced to drink in the cave.

questions.question_text: Which single dark ritual uses ingredients described in its incantation as 'unknowingly given,' 'willingly given,' and 'forcibly taken'?
questions.correct_answer: The potion used to resurrect Lord Voldemort in the graveyard
distractors: The spell used to create a Horcrux
The process of casting the Killing Curse
questions.explanation: The bone, flesh, and blood used in Voldemort's rebirth potion are each obtained in one of these three distinct ways.

questions.question_text: Which single escape plan involves Harry's own hair, six Polyjuice decoys, and disguises lasting only about an hour each?
questions.correct_answer: The 'Seven Potters' escape from Privet Drive
distractors: The rescue from the Chamber of Secrets
questions.explanation: All three details belong to the elaborate Polyjuice-based plan to smuggle Harry safely away from the Dursleys' house.

questions.question_text: What is a general, functional definition of a 'sopophorous bean' in Potions terms?
questions.correct_answer: A bean whose juice induces drowsiness or sleep when used in a potion
distractors: A bean that cures hiccups instantly
A bean used only for its bright color
questions.explanation: Sopophorous beans are a key sleep-inducing ingredient, notably used in the Draught of Living Death.

questions.question_text: What does Snape imply is required to brew the Wolfsbane Potion correctly each month for Lupin?
questions.correct_answer: Considerable skill and effort, as it is an unusually complex potion
distractors: Almost no effort at all, since it is quite simple
A specially imported cauldron from abroad
Assistance from at least one other qualified brewer
questions.explanation: Snape's grudging but consistent effort to brew Wolfsbane for Lupin reflects how demanding the potion is to get right.

questions.question_text: What remedy does Hermione get Harry to soak his hand in after Umbridge's cursed quill wounds him repeatedly during detention?
questions.explanation: Hermione treats Harry's cut, scarring hand with Essence of Murtlap to soothe the wound left by Umbridge's quill.

questions.question_text: Which of these potions does Harry encounter and smell in Slughorn's classroom but is never actually shown drinking at any point in the series?
questions.explanation: Harry smells Amortentia during Slughorn's demonstration but is never depicted drinking it himself.

questions.question_text: Within the same stretch of Half-Blood Prince, how many times is Ron accidentally poisoned by something Potions-related, first by a misdirected love potion and then by tainted mead?
distractors: Not at all; he avoids both incidents
questions.explanation: Ron first falls victim to a love potion meant for Harry, then very nearly dies after drinking poisoned mead meant for Dumbledore.

questions.question_text: Of the three ingredients in Voldemort's rebirth potion, which one is the only one NOT taken from someone alive at the time of the ritual?
questions.correct_answer: Bone of the father, taken from a grave
distractors: None; all three come from living sources
questions.explanation: Tom Riddle Sr. is long dead, so his bone comes from his grave, unlike the flesh and blood taken from living Wormtail and Harry.

questions.question_text: In what order are the three ingredients added to the cauldron during Voldemort's rebirth ritual?
distractors: All three are added at the same time
questions.explanation: The ritual proceeds in the order given in the incantation: bone of the father first, flesh of the servant second, and blood of the enemy last.

questions.question_text: What unusual infusion do Luna Lovegood and her father drink, believing it wards off Wrackspurts?
questions.explanation: Luna and Xenophilius Lovegood are fond of Gurdyroot infusion, which they believe clears the mind of Wrackspurts.

questions.question_text: Which potion does Umbridge demand Snape supply so she can interrogate Harry about the Headmaster's office mirror, only to be refused?
questions.explanation: Umbridge wants Veritaserum to force information out of Harry, but Snape claims he has none available.

questions.question_text: What excuse does Snape give Umbridge for having no Veritaserum on hand when she demands some to use on Harry?
questions.correct_answer: He claims he used his entire remaining supply on Barty Crouch Jr.
distractors: He claims it takes a year to brew and none is ready
He claims Dumbledore confiscated his entire stock
He claims Veritaserum is banned by new Ministry decree
questions.explanation: Snape slyly tells Umbridge that his last batch of Veritaserum was used up during Barty Crouch Jr.'s interrogation the previous year.

questions.question_text: According to Luna, what invisible pest does she warn Harry commonly infests mistletoe at Slughorn's Christmas party?
questions.explanation: Luna cautions Harry about Nargles lurking in the mistletoe during the Slug Club Christmas party.

questions.question_text: Is a genuine Potions use for Blast-Ended Skrewt secretions ever confirmed anywhere in the books?
questions.correct_answer: No, despite student rumors, no such use is ever confirmed
distractors: Yes, they're used in the Draught of Peace
Yes, they're a key Polyjuice ingredient
Yes, Hagrid sells them to Slughorn for potions
questions.explanation: Blast-Ended Skrewts are treated as a Care of Magical Creatures curiosity, and canon never confirms any actual Potions application for them.

questions.question_text: Which potion do anxious students reportedly take before O.W.L. and N.E.W.T. exams to sharpen their focus?
questions.explanation: Nervous exam-takers are said to rely on the Wit-Sharpening Potion to boost their mental focus before big tests.

questions.question_text: Which Hufflepuff student takes so many Calming Draughts before her O.W.L.s that she has to be revived before the exam can even begin?
questions.explanation: Hannah Abbott overdoses on Calming Draughts out of nerves and must be roused before her O.W.L. exam.

questions.question_text: What effect do the excessive Calming Draughts actually have on Hannah Abbott before her O.W.L. Potions exam?
questions.correct_answer: They leave her so drowsy she must be revived before she can begin
distractors: They make her unusually aggressive and combative
They cause her to forget the entire syllabus
They have no visible effect at all
questions.explanation: Rather than calming her, the overdose of Calming Draughts leaves Hannah too drowsy to function until she is roused.

questions.question_text: Which direction are students meant to stir the Draught of Peace, according to the instructions Harry struggles to recall during his O.W.L. exam?
distractors: Stirring is not required at all
questions.explanation: During the O.W.L. practical, Harry anxiously tries to remember whether the Draught of Peace should be stirred clockwise or counter-clockwise.

questions.question_text: Which single professor is both Head of Slytherin House and the one who brews Wolfsbane Potion every month for a werewolf colleague?
questions.explanation: Snape's dual role as Slytherin's Head and Lupin's reluctant potion-brewer are both established in Prisoner of Azkaban.

questions.question_text: What does Professor Sprout have advanced Herbology students do with Screechsnaps, beyond simply pruning them for safety?
questions.correct_answer: Study how their berries can be harvested for potion ingredients once trimmed safely
distractors: Feed them exclusively on Doxy eggs
Keep them permanently frozen to prevent screeching
questions.explanation: Screechsnaps are cultivated as part of advanced Herbology work, requiring careful, protected handling before their useful parts can be harvested.

questions.question_text: Which of these is true about the Draught of Living Death and the unnamed potion guarding the cave Horcrux?
questions.correct_answer: They are unrelated potions, despite both inducing extreme, dangerous states
distractors: They share an identical ingredient list
The cave potion is simply a diluted Draught of Living Death
questions.explanation: Although both potions are dramatic and dangerous, nothing in canon links the Draught of Living Death to the cave's unnamed potion.

questions.question_text: Which single ingredient does Snape identify for first-years as coming from a goat's stomach, and which Harry later force-feeds to a dying Ron?
questions.explanation: The very antidote introduced in Harry's first Potions lesson becomes the thing that saves Ron's life years later.

questions.question_text: According to Slughorn's classroom lecture, what can Amortentia never do, no matter how well it is brewed?
distractors: Be detected by its smell alone
Be brewed by a student under NEWT level
Affect more than one person at a time
questions.explanation: Slughorn is explicit that Amortentia can only simulate powerful infatuation, never real love.

questions.question_text: What does Snape's very first classroom description reveal is unusual about how Potions class works, compared to other subjects?
questions.correct_answer: It involves little foolish wand-waving, focusing instead on precision brewing
distractors: It requires no textbooks of any kind
It has no practical component, only theory
It is taught entirely without a teacher present
questions.explanation: Snape emphasizes that Potions relies on careful technique rather than wandwork, unlike most other subjects at Hogwarts.

questions.question_text: Which single plant is Neville given by his great-uncle Algie, later shown sporting throbbing boil-like swellings, and eventually used as a weapon during the Battle of the Department of Mysteries?
questions.explanation: Neville's unusual gift from his great-uncle Algie turns out to be more than a curiosity when he uses it to spray Stinksap at a Death Eater.

questions.question_text: Which ingredient's absence, rather than its presence, is the trick behind Harry's top-marked antidote answer in Slughorn's class?
questions.correct_answer: He skips the complex antidote-making entirely and just names a bezoar
distractors: He omits the poison sample from his test tube
He leaves out the stirring instructions
He forgets to label his phial, yet still scores well
questions.explanation: Rather than following Golpalott's Third Law to build a proper antidote, Harry's shortcut answer of 'just add a bezoar' earns him full marks.

questions.question_text: Which single potion's recipe requires both powdered moonstone and sprigs of valerian, and can prove dangerous if brewed incorrectly during an O.W.L. exam?
questions.explanation: The Draught of Peace calls for both powdered moonstone and valerian, and a mistake while brewing it can send the drinker into a dangerous sleep.

questions.question_text: Which of these Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes products is designed with two differently-colored ends serving opposite purposes, unlike Nosebleed Nougat or Fever Fudge?
questions.explanation: Puking Pastilles are unique among the Skiving Snackbox line for having one end that sickens and another that reverses the effect.

questions.question_text: Which single character teaches Potions to both Lily Evans in his own school days and to her son Harry decades later?
questions.explanation: Slughorn's long tenure connects him to both generations, having favored Lily as a student long before teaching Harry.

questions.question_text: What is peculiar about how Devil's Snare is classified, given its extremely dangerous behavior toward struggling victims?
questions.correct_answer: It is nonetheless a real plant taught about in standard Herbology curriculum, not a uniquely forbidden one
distractors: It is entirely fictional even within the books, invented only for the trapdoor challenge
It can only be grown outside of Britain
It is classified as an animal, not a plant, due to its movement
questions.explanation: Despite guarding the Philosopher's Stone, Devil's Snare is a real plant students study, as Hermione's classroom knowledge proves.

questions.question_text: Which single scene involves an unnamed potion, a self-refilling stone basin, and a small cup used to force-feed the drinker?
questions.correct_answer: Dumbledore and Harry retrieving the fake locket Horcrux in the cave
distractors: The brewing of Veritaserum for Barty Crouch Jr.'s interrogation
The rebirth ritual in the Little Hangleton graveyard
Slughorn's memory of young Tom Riddle
questions.explanation: All three details belong to the harrowing scene in the cave where Dumbledore is forced to drink the potion guarding the locket.

questions.question_text: Which of these is NOT one of the genuine ingredients in Hermione's Polyjuice Potion recipe?
questions.explanation: Dragon claw is never mentioned in Hermione's actual Polyjuice recipe; knotgrass, bicorn horn, and fluxweed all are.

questions.question_text: Which single potion's overdose can cause giddy overconfidence and singing, and whose excess effects Slughorn says peppermint can counteract?
questions.explanation: Both the overdose symptoms and the peppermint remedy belong to the same potion demonstrated in Slughorn's class.

questions.question_text: According to canon, does Neville Longbottom ever successfully brew a Draught of Living Death that rivals Harry's Prince-aided attempt?
questions.correct_answer: No; Neville is never shown matching Harry's result in that particular lesson
distractors: Yes, he ties with Harry for the top mark
Yes, he brews an even better version using his own notes
Yes, but only after switching partners with Hermione
questions.explanation: The lesson focuses on Harry's surprising success thanks to the Prince's notes; Neville is not depicted rivaling that result.

questions.question_text: Which ingredient actually causes painful boils if it touches bare skin, rather than being a cure-for-boils ingredient itself?
questions.explanation: It's a common mix-up: the Cure for Boils is made from ordinary ingredients like nettles and slugs, while raw Bubotuber pus is what actually causes boils if mishandled.
questions.source_ref: Philosopher's Stone / Order of the Phoenix

questions.question_text: Which of these potions is Ron Weasley never personally shown drinking or being affected by across the series: Felix Felicis, a love potion, or Veritaserum?
distractors: Ron is affected by all three at some point
questions.explanation: Ron believes he's drunk Felix Felicis and is genuinely dosed with a love potion, but he is never shown drinking Veritaserum.

questions.question_text: Which single plant does Professor Sprout have students in fifth year begin squeezing for pus that is later bottled and sold as an acne treatment?
questions.explanation: Fifth-year Herbology introduces students to squeezing Bubotubers, whose pus is bottled as an acne remedy once processed.

questions.question_text: Is Fluffy, the three-headed dog guarding the Philosopher's Stone, ever described as a magical plant or Herbology specimen?
questions.correct_answer: No, Fluffy is a magical creature, unrelated to Herbology entirely
distractors: Yes, he is classified as an animated Venomous Tentacula
Yes, Hagrid describes him as a rare carnivorous plant
Yes, Devil's Snare and Fluffy are the same organism
questions.explanation: Fluffy is purely a Care of Magical Creatures-style beast, kept quite separate from the Herbology-based obstacles like Devil's Snare.

questions.question_text: Which Polyjuice Potion ingredient must be stewed for a period measured in weeks, rather than being the one picked specifically during a full moon?
questions.explanation: Fluxweed must be picked during a full moon, while it's the lacewing flies that require three weeks of stewing — two separate requirements for two different ingredients.

questions.question_text: Which of these best describes Dumbledore's physical state immediately before Harry force-feeds him the last of the cave potion?
questions.correct_answer: He is gravely weakened and pleading for water, seemingly hallucinating
distractors: He is completely unconscious and unresponsive throughout
He shows no visible distress at all
He appears to be laughing uncontrollably
questions.explanation: Dumbledore is shown in visible agony, begging for water and seemingly reliving painful memories as he is forced to keep drinking.

questions.question_text: Which single ingredient does Harry recall from his very first Potions lesson that later becomes the subject of Slughorn's more advanced antidote lesson years afterward?
questions.explanation: The humble bezoar, first mentioned by Snape in year one, resurfaces as Harry's clever shortcut in Slughorn's sixth-year antidote lesson.

questions.question_text: Which of these is true regarding Neville Longbottom's Potions versus Herbology performance across the series?
questions.correct_answer: He consistently struggles in Potions but shows real skill and confidence in Herbology
distractors: He excels equally in both subjects throughout
He struggles in both subjects equally
He excels in Potions but struggles in Herbology
questions.explanation: Neville's contrasting performance is a recurring detail: weak in Potions, notably strong in Herbology.

questions.question_text: Which single Herbology plant requires protective earmuffs both as an infant being repotted and, according to O.W.L.-era lessons, poses a fatal risk once fully mature?
questions.explanation: Mandrakes are dangerous at every stage: a young one's cry can knock you out, while a mature one's cry can kill.

questions.question_text: Which of these ingredients is genuinely part of the Shrinking Solution recipe: rat spleen, phoenix feather, or unicorn horn?
distractors: None of these are part of the recipe
questions.explanation: Rat spleen, alongside shrivelfig and daisy roots, is a genuine ingredient in the Shrinking Solution.

questions.question_text: Which single plant, described as having a piercing scream, is used both to cure Petrification and to teach first-years about dangerous Herbology specimens?
questions.explanation: Mandrakes serve double duty in the books: a curriculum staple that teaches caution, and the literal cure for the Basilisk's petrifying gaze.

questions.question_text: Which of these best explains why Slughorn attends the funeral of Aragog the Acromantula?
questions.correct_answer: He hopes to secretly collect the giant spider's valuable venom
distractors: He was a close personal friend of Aragog's for decades
He is required to attend as a Ministry official
He wants to study Aragog's web-spinning for a Charms project
questions.explanation: Slughorn's true motive is far less sentimental than it appears: he's after Aragog's venom as a rare Potions ingredient.

questions.question_text: Which single potion connects Snape's monthly brewing duties for Lupin, a smoking appearance when delivered, and a demanding, complex recipe few wizards can manage?
questions.explanation: All three details describe the Wolfsbane Potion Snape reluctantly but skillfully brews for Lupin each month.

questions.question_text: Which of these potions or substances is explicitly stated to have no known antidote anywhere in the books?
distractors: Most common poisons, per the bezoar's usefulness
The Draught of Living Death, thanks to Wiggenweld-type remedies
Basilisk venom, thanks to phoenix tears
questions.explanation: Unlike common poisons (cured by a bezoar) or Basilisk venom (cured by phoenix tears), no antidote to Veritaserum is ever described.
